# Download attachment — `redmine_download_attachment`

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-tools-doc.ts from the tool registry. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run gen:tools`. -->

_write_

Download a Redmine attachment and save it into a local directory. Find the id with `redmine_get_issue` using `include: ["attachments"]`. The file is written into `save_path` under the attachment's own name unless you override `filename`. The destination must be inside the operator-configured REDMINE_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES, and an existing file is never overwritten — the call fails instead, so pass a different `filename` or directory to retry. Returns where the file was saved, its name, and its size in bytes.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attachment_id` | integer | **yes** | Numeric id of the attachment. Get it from `redmine_get_issue` with `include: ["attachments"]`, which lists each attachment id, filename, and size. |
| `save_path` | string | **yes** | Destination **directory** — the filename is appended to it, so do not include one. It must resolve inside the operator-allowlisted REDMINE_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES. |
| `filename` | string | no | Name to save the file under. Defaults to the attachment's own filename. Any directory part is stripped: only a bare filename is honoured. |

## Example

```json
{
  "name": "redmine_download_attachment",
  "arguments": {
    "attachment_id": 42,
    "save_path": "text",
    "filename": "text"
  }
}
```
